console_float.name: Option A: console pocket (recommended)
console_float.summary: The printed enclosure sits in front of the console opening. Its 205.6 × 129 mm bezel spans the opening's full height (its top edge stays under the HVAC panel) and overhangs the 191 / 123 mm sides. The 112 × 124 × 50.5 mm rear box with the Pi 4 and the carrier PCB drops into the pocket: it needs ≥ 56 mm of clear depth, and the car's USB / 12 V strip is behind it (measure with the foam mock-up). The screen sits 8 mm toward the driver and the frame stands ~22 mm proud of the trim: check the shifter in P. Air: slots beside the screen → behind the display → lid fan → 2 mm gap round the plate.
console_float.ergonomics: Low and shaded (cooler); you glance down. The amber LEDs at the mirrors and the unit's beep do the alerting.
console_float.display_cable: HDMI flat cable from the TS-7's right edge through the plate to the Pi's HDMI0; touch and 5 V on one split micro-USB lead (5 V from J5, data to a Pi USB port)

dash_top.name: Option B: dash top on a RAM / AMPS mount
dash_top.summary: The same enclosure on a RAM-B-202U round base, screwed to the AMPS 30 × 38 mm M4 nuts in the box's bottom wall: an eye-level glance. More sun (250 cd/m² washes out) and heat (the TS-7 is rated −10…+60 °C, storage +70 °C), so take it in on hot days. Keep clear of the passenger airbag door and the windshield view.
dash_top.ergonomics: Fastest glance; worst sun and heat.
dash_top.display_cable: HDMI flat cable from the TS-7's right edge through the plate to the Pi's HDMI0; touch and 5 V on one split micro-USB lead (5 V from J5, data to a Pi USB port)

pcb6_stackup.role: Parts; the high-current straps (12 V input chain, both bucks, 5 V to J5) laid before routing; signals; power pours and a GND pour in the gaps. Thermal reliefs on every through-hole pad

Signals, power pours under the bucks and the 12 V chain (stitched to L1), and GND pour stitched to L1; faces the Pi with a 3 mm air gap (pins ≤ 2.5 mm); its silkscreen carries the signature: the AjayaDesign logo over “Designed by Ajaya Dahal for his Basanti 2018, Toyota Yaris iA”

wiring_harness.name: Left mirror camera (USB UVC)
wiring_harness.route: Lower mirror cap, aimed ~39° outward of straight back and ~10° down on a printed wedge (a strip of the car's side at the picture's inner edge) → service loop through the mirror hinge → door harness → factory door boot (silicone grease) → kick panel → under the console trim → the Pi's USB 2.0 port through the enclosure's window (90° adapter)
wiring_harness.cable: The camera's own USB 2.0 lead (~3 m), not cut; or spliced with the pairs twisted and the shield continuous. No JST-GH in the data path
wiring_harness.protection: O-ring + neutral-cure RTV at the cap, drip loop, butyl on the door's vapour barrier, ferrite at the Pi; drill clear of the mirror's LED turn-signal repeater and its wires

wiring_harness.name: Right mirror camera (USB UVC)
wiring_harness.route: Lower mirror cap, same ~39° outward / ~10° down wedge → hinge service loop → passenger door harness → door boot → kick panel → behind the glovebox → the Pi's second USB 2.0 port (90° adapter)
wiring_harness.cable: The camera's own USB 2.0 lead (~3.5 m), same rules as the left
wiring_harness.protection: Same as the left side; drill clear of the mirror's LED turn-signal repeater and its wires

wiring_harness.name: 12 V ACC feed (one fuse tap)
wiring_harness.route: Driver's interior fuse box: Add-A-Circuit (5 A) on a non-critical ACC fuse, metered first (hot in ACC and ON, dead with the key out; never SRS or engine) → ring terminal on a chassis ground stud → under the dash → J1 screw terminal on the carrier, through the lid's cable exit
wiring_harness.protection: 4 A fuse + SMCJ24CA + −60 V P-MOSFET reverse protection + π filter on the board. ACC only: zero draw when parked, by construction

wiring_harness.name: 5 V / 5 A to the Pi and the display (inside the enclosure)
wiring_harness.route: J5 (5.08 mm screw terminal, 3 × 5 V / GND) → 90° USB-C pigtail to the Pi; second pair → the display's 5 V on its split micro-USB lead; third pair spare. The lid fan is on J8 (5V_ESP)
wiring_harness.protection: 470 µF at the Pi end; the carrier's TPS54560B buck at 5.17 V (5 A) with a 10 mΩ shunt and an INA226 on it; pass = vcgencmd get_throttled 0x0 under load

wiring_harness.name: Display: HDMI flat cable + split micro-USB lead (enclosure and pocket)
wiring_harness.route: TS-7 right edge: straight HDMI-A FPC adapter + 90° micro-USB plug → up the bezel's right cavity → the plate's cable slot → the pocket beside the box → the slot above the USB window → flat cable to a straight micro-HDMI adapter in the Pi's HDMI0. The micro-USB lead splits: 5 V + GND → J5 pair 2; D+ / D− + GND → 90° USB-A plug in a blue USB 3.0 port through the window
wiring_harness.cable: 20 cm HDMI flat cable (FPC kit); 4-wire micro-USB lead ~30 cm
wiring_harness.protection: Red (VBUS) wire cut on the Pi's leg, so the two 5 V sources never meet; strain relief at both plugs; the flat cable kept away from the antenna lead (bench test B6)

wiring_harness.name: Left / right turn-signal sense (IO36 / IO39)
wiring_harness.route: Each mirror's LED turn-signal repeater feed, at the mirror connector inside the door (left mirror = left signal), found with the wiring diagram and confirmed with a meter (flashing 12 V with that side's signal and the hazards) → solder + heat-shrink → twisted pair alongside the camera cable through the door boot → the PC817 inputs on the carrier. Fallbacks: the kick-panel feed, or the rear amber WY21W turn bulbs
wiring_harness.cable: 22 AWG pair, ~2.5 m per side (door to console)
wiring_harness.protection: 2 × 1.1 kΩ + 1N4148 per input (~6 mA, isolated). Firmware bridges PWM gaps, rejects spikes and recognises hazards

wiring_harness.name: Pi ↔ ESP32 link (inside the enclosure): UART + I2C
wiring_harness.route: Pi GPIO header → your 40-pin ribbon (IDC, red stripe on pin 1; conductor n = pin n) → conductors 6 GND, 8 TXD, 10 RXD, 12 GPIO18, 15 SDA6, 16 SCL6 joined to a 6-pin GH-to-Dupont pigtail → J6 on the carrier → UART2 IO16 / IO17, and the carrier's I2C bus through Q901 / Q902 while GPIO18 is high
wiring_harness.cable: 40-pin ribbon (~10 cm, IDC ~12.5 mm tall) + 20 cm GH-6 pigtail
wiring_harness.protection: UART: 1 k / 4.7 k series, the ESP32 keeps TX off while the Pi is unpowered, checksummed lines. I2C: two 2N7002 switches only the Pi's GPIO18 turns on (off while the Pi is off, halted or booting), Pi-side pull-ups powered by GPIO18; one master at a time

wiring_harness.name: Left / right amber blind-spot LEDs
wiring_harness.route: Carrier JST-GH → with the camera cable through each door boot → LED in the inner door sail (inside the cabin), facing the driver. Not in the A-pillar trim (curtain airbag), not on the outside of the mirror (an amber light seen from behind isn't allowed: VC 25950(b))
wiring_harness.protection: Low-side MOSFET + series resistor; PWM level set by the Pi for night dimming. Steady = vehicle there, flashing = you are signalling towards it

wiring_harness.name: 12 V piezo (inside the dash unit)
wiring_harness.route: Carrier J4 JST-GH (BUZ+, BUZ−; the BTN pins stay free) → out of the box with the display leads → up the bezel's right cavity → the piezo on three fingers behind the right intake slots. No lead outside the unit
wiring_harness.protection: 33 Ω + SMAJ18A on the 12 V feed. Danger beeps at once and after 3 s, then the LED alone from 4 s; TPMS beeps and reminds twice; a fault beeps once. Mute from the touch screen

wiring_harness.name: 2× Car USB passthroughs (from v1) in the twin USB wing
wiring_harness.route: Both sockets stacked in the printed twin wing on the bezel's right edge (39 mm pitch), facing the passenger → lower cable climbs behind the centre screw post inside the wing; both enter the bezel through one side opening → cross above the display's plugs → drop through the plate's cable slot → car USB ports / flush 12 V charger in the pocket
wiring_harness.cable: Both passthrough cables (Ø ~5.5 mm each, measure them)
wiring_harness.protection: None needed: they only extend the car's own ports. Plug both into the pocket ports before the unit goes home

wiring_harness.name: GPS: fallback speed source (NEO-M8N)
wiring_harness.route: GPS puck on the dash top under the windshield (needs sky) → behind the instrument panel (not through the A-pillar trim) → carrier JST-GH (UART1 IO33 / IO27, 5 V)
wiring_harness.protection: Speed gate: the OBD-II speed first while the dongle answers, else GPS; both lost: last decision held 10 s, then LEDs only

wiring_harness.name: OBD-II speed: your Bluetooth dongle (optional)
wiring_harness.route: OBD-II port under the dash, driver's side → Bluetooth Classic → the ESP32 in the enclosure (no wires)
wiring_harness.cable: None: a low-profile dongle, or a short right-angle extension tied up out of the footwell
wiring_harness.protection: Requests PID 0x0D only, never listens to the bus; counts while < 1 s old, then the GPS takes over; parked drain measured first (B8). Not used for the blinker

wiring_harness.name: 315 MHz TPMS (4 × EG53MA4 → CC1101)
wiring_harness.route: CC1101's own SMA → 10 cm RG316 → SMA bulkhead in the enclosure wall → 30 cm RG316 → 315 MHz whip clear of the Pi, the display and the camera cables
wiring_harness.protection: 315 MHz-tuned CC1101 module; noise floor checked with everything on and off (bench test B6)

wiring_harness.name: Phase 2: CAN (no PCB change)
wiring_harness.route: OBD-II port → CANable-type USB adapter (gs_usb / SocketCAN) → a Pi USB port
wiring_harness.protection: Listen-only: never transmits. HS-CAN (pins 6/14): wheel speeds, gear, and the blinker broadcast 0x9A as a cross-check of the lamp taps (opendbc IDs, to confirm on this car)

checklist_bench.text: B4: Pi + display (on J5 pair 2) + cameras + fan, CPU stress 30 min
checklist_bench.where: Pass: get_throttled 0x0, >= 4.95 V at the Pi's GPIO 5 V pin under load, regulator < 80 °C

checklist_bench.text: B5: AM radio next to the running setup
B6: CC1101 noise floor with everything off, then on (display and its HDMI flat cable included)
B7: TS-7 on HDMI-A-1 at 1024 × 600, power and touch over the split lead, the Pi and the display on one 5 V source: 10 cold starts, the four corners, ddcutil detect
checklist_bench.where: Pass: picture every start (else video=HDMI-A-1:1024x600@60D in cmdline.txt), touch accurate with the cameras streaming; note whether DDC/CI dimming works (else a dark UI at night)

checklist_bench.text: B8: OBD dongle: parked current; ESP32 ↔ dongle over Bluetooth with the TPMS decoder running; optional ATCRA 09A sniff while signalling
checklist_bench.where: Pass: < ~5 mA parked; speed within ~3 s and matching the speedometer; TPMS decode rate unchanged

checklist_bench.text: T1: in the printed enclosure, in a sun-soaked car, vision app 30 min
Host tests and audits: test_logic (166 checks), check_pinmap.py (+ --selftest), make_enclosure.py (63 checks), make_mounts.py (28 checks), sync_plan.py --check; run_checks.py re-runs them all

checklist_tools.text: Plastic trim tools, 10 mm socket, Phillips #1 / #2, 2 mm and 2.5 mm hex keys
Preciva PR-3254 (in the lab) for the Dupont crimps where the GH pigtail meets the Pi's ribbon. No JST-GH crimper: the elechawk pigtails come pre-crimped, and power goes to screw terminals
Soldering iron, 60–80 W, with a fine tip and a chisel tip (ground pins tie into the top/bottom pours through thermal reliefs), flux, heat-shrink, heat gun
Step drill and a deburring tool for the mirror caps (practise on a spare cap)
Printer that does ASA / ABS (enclosed), or order MJF PA12
Caliper (fit template, TS-7 dimensions, part sizes)

build_steps.text: Drive with rtl_433 -f 315M (wake each wheel with the OEC-T5) and log the four EG53MA4 tyre IDs; check the v1 decoder on the capture.
TS-7 + Pi 4 on the bench: Bookworm finds it on HDMI-A-1 (1024 × 600); touch over USB; try DDC/CI brightness with ddcutil (B7).
Optional: identify your OBD-II dongle (Classic or BLE, PIN, MAC), read the speed with a phone app, measure its parked current (B8a). It feeds the speed gate only, never the blinker.
Two inventory USB cameras on the Pi: capture thread + 320 × 320 detector; measure the frame rate (V1) before buying car cameras.
Breadboard ESP32 + CC1101 + GPS + two blinker switches + piezo; run the v2 logic (166 host checks already pass) against the Pi over the UART protocol.
Print the fit template; tape a 112 × 124 × 51 mm foam block behind the bezel outline; check the pocket depth, the shifter in P and the HVAC knobs in the car (G5).

Measure the TS-7 (fit template page 1) and the plugs; regenerate (make_enclosure.py, 63 checks) and the template; print the bezel and hang the display in it, then the housing, lid and USB wing in ASA (G6).

Print the carrier's 1:1 assembly drawing and set the sockets and terminals on it; measure your DevKit's row spacing; then order at JLCPCB: 2 layers, 1.6 mm, 1 oz, lead-free HASL, tented vias, Economic PCBA on 2 of 5 (169 placements, 51 BOM lines — merchandise < $59.00 so Global Standard Direct Line unlocks); the quote must read 100 × 100 mm (G7, G8; carrier README).

When the boards arrive: hand-solder the 8 SMD parts first (one LCSC order; flux, 60–80 W chisel tip), then the 5 THT connectors — DevKit and CC1101 sockets (DevKit row to match yours), screw terminals (2 + 3 blue 2-pole blocks) and fan header; check the polarized parts.
Bring-up on a current-limited supply (carrier README): rails, EN delay, inhibit, reverse polarity, I2C scan (0x20, 0x40, 0x41, 0x48), 1–5 A on J5; then B1–B3 (G4).
Pi + TS-7 + both cameras on the carrier: B4 measured at the Pi's GPIO 5 V pin, B5 with an AM radio (RT rework if it whines), B6 radio noise floor with everything on.

ESP32 application around the tested logic (02-firmware/v2), started on a breadboard while the boards are made: the CC1101 driver and EG53MA4 decoder from bringup/ with carrier-sense gating (RF-01), GPS NMEA, BluetoothSerial for the OBD-II dongle (B8b), LEDC PWM for the LEDs, the piezo patterns, Pi power sequencing, UART2 to the Pi and a Wi-Fi OTA service mode (ESP-01). Flash it over the DevKit's USB.

Pi app: two-camera capture and detector (V1 sets the model and frame rate), the 1024 × 600 touch UI (a camera only on the blinker or a danger; nothing needs touch while moving: D5, V8, S3, DSP-09), the UART link with the touch screen's mute counter (LNK-07) and the link's set-up lines (dtoverlay=i2c6, gpio=18=op,dl: the Pi stays off the I2C bus until the ESP32 hands it over), the first-month logging mode.

Cameras into the mirror caps: mark the turn repeater and its wires inside the cap before drilling, then O-ring + neutral-cure RTV. Cables through the hinges and door boots with service loops, tied to the factory harness on the dry side, clear of the window glass and its regulator; reseal the vapour barriers with butyl; LEDs in the door sails. Cycle door / window / mirror 50 times.

One Add-A-Circuit on an ACC fuse slot metered in ACC, ON and START (hot side feeding both fuses) + chassis ground stud; blinker feeds from the wiring diagram, metered (G9); GPS on the dash top (fallback speed); the OBD dongle in its port if it passed B8.

Enclosure into the pocket (or onto the RAM base): both USB passthrough cables into the pocket USB ports / 12 V charger first, 90° USB adapters, harness through the grommet, antenna lead out; VHB on the twin USB wing's back edges so it lands flat on the trim; never seal the gap round the plate.
Mark the blind-spot zones on the touch screen with a car parked in each lane; check the mirror-alignment reference; T1 thermal test in a hot car.
Read-only root on; road test by day, at night, on the highway, in rain and in a parking lot (quiet below 8 mph); all four tyres reporting.

premortem.title: HS-CAN on ESP32 GPIO2 plus an MCP2515 on IO15 for MS-CAN
premortem.cause: GPIO2 must be low at reset or serial flashing fails, and a CAN receiver idles high. The MCP2515 also needs an interrupt pin, and no pins were left
premortem.fix: CAN moves to a USB CAN adapter (CANable / gs_usb) on the Pi in phase 2: SocketCAN, listen-only, no PCB change

premortem.title: Power latch from 12 V BAT with an "OR gate" and a "30 s hardware watchdog"
premortem.cause: Never designed; a stuck latch flattens the battery, and the ESP32 controlled the Pi's power
premortem.fix: ACC-only power (P1). No latch, no battery tap, zero draw parked by construction. A read-only root makes hard power-off safe

premortem.title: The ESP32 enables the Pi rail
premortem.cause: Flashing the ESP32 from the Pi resets it, the rail drops, the Pi dies mid-flash: deadlock
premortem.fix: The Pi buck is on by default with ACC (its EN divider pulls it up, after a 1.2–1.4 s delay). The ESP32 can only delay it (PIN_PI_INHIBIT, a 2N7002 pulled down), and it reads the rail-up sense first, so a reset with the Pi running never cuts it (audit FW-02)

premortem.title: Pololu D36V50F5 treated as a 36 V part
premortem.cause: Pololu's page: 5.5–50 V in, reverse protection to 40 V, ~5.5 A, EN on by default, 3 A per header pin; and a fixed 5.0 V ±4 % output that can leave the Pi at its undervoltage threshold (PWR-01)
premortem.fix: Replaced by a TPS54560B buck on the carrier: 60 V in, 5 A, set to 5.17 V; the ESP32 side has a second one

premortem.title: 1.5KE24CA TVS
premortem.cause: Minimum breakdown 22.8 V: it conducts on a 24 V jump start and burns
premortem.fix: SMCJ24CA: 26.7 V minimum breakdown, 38.9 V clamp, 1500 W, bidirectional. Everything after it is rated ≥ 40 V

premortem.title: (implied) series Schottky for reverse polarity
premortem.cause: ~1 W at 2.5 A in an SMA package
premortem.fix: P-MOSFET reverse protection: SUD50P06-15, −60 V (the audit raised it from the −40 V AOD4185, PWR-02), gate held at −5 V by a divider (−16 V at a 39 V clamp)

premortem.title: Blind-spot LEDs in the "A-pillar mirror-sail triangles, zero door-boot wires"
premortem.cause: The Yaris iA has side-curtain airbags behind the A-pillar trim, and the triangle at the mirror base belongs to the door
premortem.fix: LEDs on the inner door sail, inside the cabin, wired with the camera cable through the door boot. Not on the outside of the mirror: in California a lamp visible from the rear must be red unless it is a turn signal or a few others (VC 25950(b); audit SAF-08). Nothing in the A-pillar trim or on the dash top

premortem.title: Piezo under the steering-column lower shroud
premortem.cause: Next to the collapsible column and the knee-bolster area
premortem.fix: Inside the dash unit, on three fingers behind the bezel's right intake slots: no lead outside the unit (it first went into a wired pod by the shifter, now dropped)

premortem.title: Bi-colour amber/red LEDs
premortem.cause: Red light near the windshield is a legal grey zone and isn't the OEM convention
premortem.fix: Amber only: steady = vehicle in the blind spot, flashing = you are signalling towards it

premortem.title: "50 Ω microstrip from the CC1101 to an SMA" on the PCB
premortem.cause: The module has its own SMA; there is no RF trace
premortem.fix: Module at the board edge with its SMA overhanging; ground plane under it

premortem.title: Pi 4 M2.5 hole pattern (58 × 49 mm) so the PCB can stack behind the Pi
premortem.cause: Those holes land under the ESP32 DevKit and the CC1101, and stacking blocks the Pi's fan and USB
premortem.fix: Dropped from rev A; 4 × M3 on 92 × 92 mm only

premortem.title: The 7" display "floats in the pocket and clears the shifter"
premortem.cause: A 7" display is wider than the pocket: the TS-7's board is 165.3 mm wide (the Official display's glass 192.96), the opening 191 mm at the top and 123 mm at the bottom
premortem.fix: It sits in front of the trim in a 205.6 × 129 mm bezel, 21.8 mm proud; only the 112 × 124 mm rear box goes into the pocket. Decide with the 1:1 mock-up

premortem.title: The display is "in inventory"
premortem.cause: The inventory lists only the Touch Display Adapter v1.1 board
premortem.fix: You have a SunFounder TS-7 (HDMI video, USB touch), not the Official display. The enclosure, harness, power budget and BOM are redrawn for it (audit DSP-01)

premortem.title: Blinker inputs on IO36 / IO39 as interrupts
premortem.cause: ESP32 errata 3.11: these pins glitch low for ~80 ns when the ADC or Wi-Fi powers up
premortem.fix: Polled at 1 kHz with an RC filter (poll tag, enforced by the audit)

premortem.title: "Mirror LED turn signals" on the Yaris iA (drawn in the viewer)
premortem.cause: Not verified at the time
premortem.fix: Verified by the audit: Toyota's MY2017/2018 Yaris iA feature pages list "power outside mirrors with LED turn signal indicators" as standard, and the owner's manual lists the side turn lights as LED. Each mirror's repeater feed is the natural blinker tap (I1), and the camera hole in the cap must miss the repeater and its wires

premortem.title: v2 still listed the v1 front-panel controls (EC11 encoder, menu buttons) plus a "camera toggle" button
premortem.cause: The 7" touch screen does menus, settings, TPMS pairing and camera calibration; the 2.7" OLED and the 4 tyre LEDs are redundant too
premortem.fix: All removed, the mute button too. The touch screen mutes and acknowledges, and every beep stops by itself (danger after 4 s while the LED keeps flashing, TPMS after two reminders, a fault beeps once), so nothing nags while the Pi boots or after it crashes. J4 keeps the button input (IO4, the v1 RC) as a spare

premortem.title: Our own fit template placed the display's M3 holes 0.65 mm off
premortem.cause: The drawing dimensions them from the outer frame flange (11.89 line), not the frame body (12.54)
premortem.fix: Fixed then for the Official display; superseded by the TS-7, which has no drawing. Its ear holes (157.3 × 114.4 mm, from photos) are a measured parameter, and the template's page 1 draws them 1:1 so you can lay the display on it

premortem.title: Display "0–50 °C, brightness not specified"
premortem.cause: The Official display's brief said 0–50 °C, its docs −20…+70 °C. Your TS-7 (SunFounder): −10…+60 °C operating, −20…+70 °C storage, 250 cd/m², IPS, 170° viewing, no documented brightness control
premortem.fix: Design for −10…+60 °C (D1); 250 cd/m² is dim in daylight (D2); IPS needs no upside-down mount (D3); dimming is a bench test (D4, B7)

premortem.title: "The Pi's USB end can face either side"
premortem.cause: Its ports must line up with the box's USB window, and its HDMI / USB-C edge must face free space for the 90° plugs
premortem.fix: The Pi sits on 4 M2.5 posts in the housing: ports to the driver's right (+X), HDMI / USB-C edge on top, GPIO header at the bottom. The window, the cable slot and the fit checks are built for that

premortem.title: Phase 2: "HS-CAN speed/reverse, MS-CAN turn signals"
premortem.cause: For the 2016–21 Mazdas that openpilot supports, the turn lamps (BLINK_INFO, 0x9A) and the stalk (TURN_SWITCH, 0x91) are on the powertrain HS-CAN, next to the speed (ENGINE_DATA, 0x202). This car uses that message family: Metasploit's mazda_ic_mover drives the Mazda 2 / Scion iA / Yaris iA cluster with one 0x202 frame
premortem.fix: Phase 2 listens on HS-CAN (OBD pins 6/14). The IDs come from opendbc's reverse-engineered mazda_2017.dbc: confirm each one on this car (B8) before relying on it

premortem.title: The key passes through ACC on the way to START; the Pi starts booting and the crank browns it out, or it boot-loops
premortem.fix: The Pi buck starts only above 8.0 V and 1.2–1.4 s after ACC (EN divider 1 MΩ / 150 kΩ + 10 µF). Firmware holds the Pi until the engine runs (≥ 13.0 V for 1 s) or 15 s in ACC

premortem.title: Battery flat after a week parked
premortem.fix: ACC-only power: nothing is connected when the key is out

premortem.title: SD card corrupted by hard power-off
premortem.fix: Read-only root (raspi-config overlay FS), journal in RAM, settings in ESP32 NVS, a high-endurance card

premortem.title: 5 V sags under load: undervoltage flag, USB cameras drop out
premortem.fix: A 5 A buck on the carrier set to 5.17 V (the Pi flags undervoltage below 4.63 V ±5 %: audit PWR-01), 2 mm copper straps, three 5 V / GND pairs on J5, 18 AWG under 0.5 m, 470 µF at the Pi end; 5V_PI rail 2.4 A typical, 3.9 A peak (with the TS-7's 0.48 A, on its own J5 pair; the lid fan is on the ESP32 rail). An INA226 logs the rail. Pass (B4) = ≥ 4.95 V at the Pi's GPIO 5 V pin under full load and get_throttled 0x0 after 30 minutes

premortem.title: Load dump, jump start, reverse battery or negative spikes kill the board
premortem.fix: Onboard 4 A fuse + SMCJ24CA (38.9 V clamp) + −60 V P-MOSFET; downstream ratings: both bucks 60 V, the INA226 40 V. A load dump above ~39 V on a car without central suppression is an accepted trade-off (as in v1)

premortem.title: AM radio buzz: the ~450 kHz bucks' harmonics fall in the AM band
premortem.fix: π filter (6.8 µH, 10 µF in, 2 × 10 µF + 47 µF out) on 12 V, a solid GND plane right under the bucks, short twisted leads, ferrites. Test with the AM radio (B5); if it buzzes, one resistor per buck (RT → 43 kΩ) moves it to ~2.2 MHz, above the band

premortem.title: A fuse tap on the wrong fuse (SRS, engine ECU) or the wrong way round
premortem.fix: One Add-A-Circuit, 5 A, on a non-critical ACC fuse. Meter it: hot in ACC and ON, dead with the key out; note whether it drops in START. Never a yellow SRS circuit

premortem.title: Hand-soldering through-hole pins or the 8 hand-solder SMD parts connected to copper pours won't wet
premortem.fix: Thermal reliefs on all through-hole pour connections and on C104's and U801's GND pads (PCB-21); the other power parts join small local pours; lead-free HASL; all 169 tiny/fine-pitch/PowerPAD SMDs are reflowed by JLCPCB PCBA; solder the remaining parts with a 60–80 W chisel tip and flux

premortem.title: 5 A power traces overheat on 1 oz copper
premortem.fix: High-current paths laid as checked 2 mm outer-layer straps plus stitched top/bottom 1 oz copper pours

premortem.title: The ESP32 back-powers an unpowered Pi through the UART
premortem.fix: 1 k / 4.7 k series resistors; firmware keeps UART TX off while the Pi rail is off

premortem.title: Opto resistors overheat on a load dump
premortem.fix: 2 × 1.1 kΩ 1206 in series per input (0.5 W), 1N4148 reverse diode

premortem.likelihood: High (the earlier drafts did it twice)
premortem.title: A strapping pin is misused: GPIO12 high at reset (wrong flash voltage), GPIO2 high (flashing fails)
premortem.fix: Pin map audit with rules for strapping, input-only, flash, boot-glitch, ADC1 and UART0 pins

premortem.title: Opening /dev/ttyUSB0 toggles DTR/RTS and resets the ESP32
premortem.fix: The runtime link is the GPIO UART (Pi GPIO14/15 ↔ ESP32 UART2); USB is only for flashing. The Pi's power no longer depends on the ESP32

premortem.title: The Pi's UART carries Bluetooth or a login console
premortem.fix: enable_uart=1, dtoverlay=disable-bt, remove console=serial0,... from cmdline.txt

premortem.title: Garbage, partial lines or a corrupted message trigger a wrong alert
premortem.fix: NMEA-style lines with XOR checksum, strict field parsing, resync on $, overlong lines dropped

premortem.title: A ground offset or noise between the boards corrupts the UART
premortem.fix: Common star ground at the regulator; 115200 Bd over < 1 m

premortem.likelihood: Medium once a Pi feature uses I2C
premortem.title: The Pi and the ESP32 both drive the shared I2C bus (J6 now carries the Pi's I2C6, switched on by its GPIO18), or the Pi's I2C wakes it from halt
premortem.fix: gpio=18=op,dl keeps the Pi off the bus from power-on. I2C6 on GPIO22/23 instead of I2C1 means no fixed pull-ups and no GPIO3 wake. One master at a time: the Pi raises GPIO18 only with the DevKit out or after a $I2C hand-over (LNK-09, LNK-10). Remove Q901/Q902 to take it off for good
premortem.status: Fixed (design); Plan: the $I2C hand-over in the firmware

premortem.title: Pi 4 too slow for two streams plus YOLO
premortem.fix: 320 × 320 NCNN, alternate sides, blinker side first, hardware JPEG decode; fall back to motion-in-ROI. Measure in phase 1 with the two USB cameras you already have, before buying cameras. Pass: ≥ 5 detections per second per side. If not, the inventory's Jetson Nano 4 GB runs the detector on its GPU (TensorRT); it drives HDMI only, so it pairs with the SunFounder display (audit CAM-04)

premortem.title: The Pi 4 has 1 GB of RAM
premortem.fix: free -h; need ≥ 2 GB

premortem.title: The Pi throttles in a hot cabin, worse inside a closed enclosure
premortem.fix: Enclosure airflow: intake slots in the bezel beside the screen → behind the display (its ~2.4 W warms the air by a few K) → the plate's three windows → past the Pi and round the PCB → 30 mm lid fan (inventory) blowing out → a 2 mm gap round the plate (bumps), so the pocket is never sealed. Heatsinks; hot-start hold (board ≥ 60 °C: wait for 55 °C, at most 10 min). Test T1 in a sun-soaked car: SoC < 80 °C, get_throttled = 0x0. If it fails: lower clock, bigger gap, or the PCB in its own box

premortem.title: No small USB camera fits under the mirror (most "mirror cameras" are analog/AHD), or the one bought can't see the whole zone
premortem.fix: Acceptance test before mounting (audit CAM-01–03): UVC MJPEG 720p30 using the full sensor width (no centre crop); HFOV ≥ 95° measured (1 m from a wall it shows ≥ 2.18 m: "90–110°" in listings is usually the diagonal); WDR (Starvis), no IR LEDs, −20…+70 °C or better (+85 °C preferred), IP67, barrel ≤ 20 mm, ≥ 3.5 m lead; both cameras streaming at once on the Pi 4 for 30 min with no -28 in dmesg (they share one USB 2.0 bus). Aim ~39° outward of straight back, ~10° down (printed wedge), with a strip of the car's side at the inner edge; check with cones at the zone's corners. Fallback: AHD cameras + a 2-channel USB capture. Measure the barrel before drilling

premortem.title: Cutting the USB cable for the door boot breaks USB 2.0 high-speed
premortem.fix: No JST-GH in the data path: splice with the pairs kept twisted and the shield continuous, or a solder-type USB-A plug. Pass = no resets in dmesg on a 30-minute drive

premortem.title: A folded or bumped mirror points the camera elsewhere; the blind-spot zone is wrong
premortem.fix: At start-up the Pi compares the car-body edge with the stored reference; on mismatch it sets camFault for that side → fault pattern on that LED, no alerts from that side
premortem.status: Fixed (protocol + ESP32 logic); Pi side to implement

premortem.title: Night, rain or low sun hides vehicles; motorcycles are tiny
premortem.fix: Starvis WDR, no IR LEDs, hydrophobic lens coating, headlight-blob fallback in the ROI, lower motorcycle threshold with persistence

premortem.title: The vision app crashes or freezes and the system fails silently
premortem.fix: systemd Restart=always + watchdog on the Pi. The ESP32 shows the fault pattern and gives one fault beep when reports stop for 1 s, when the vision frame counter (seq) stops moving while "ready" is still sent, or when a powered Pi isn't ready after 90 s. Another fault beep only after 30 s without a fault, so a flapping link doesn't nag
premortem.status: Fixed (firmware, audit FW-06/07/10); Pi side to implement

premortem.title: 20–35 s boot: no blind-spot help just after starting
premortem.fix: Lamp test when the system becomes ready, so you know when it works

premortem.title: OpenCV / NCNN / Python dependency breakage on a later image
premortem.fix: Pinned versions, a provisioning script, a golden SD-card image

premortem.title: The display is damaged by a parked car's heat
premortem.fix: The TS-7 is rated −10…+60 °C operating and −20…+70 °C storage (SunFounder), below a sun-soaked dash top. Shaded console mount preferred, sunshade, AMPS quick-release for heat waves, hot-start hold

premortem.title: Washed out in sunlight: SunFounder gives only 250 cd/m²
premortem.fix: Shaded mount; the bezel lip shades the border; full backlight by day; high-contrast UI (white on black, large icons). Test in the sun with the mock-up

premortem.title: Poor contrast from the driver's seat
premortem.fix: The TS-7 is IPS with 170° viewing, so it is mounted the normal way up and the image isn't rotated (the Official display needed the upside-down mount). Still look at it from your seat with the mock-up

premortem.title: The screen and LEDs glare at night
premortem.fix: LED level sent by the Pi (from camera exposure); optional VL6180X light sensor on I2C. The TS-7 has no documented brightness control: try DDC/CI (ddcutil) on the bench; if it doesn't answer, a dark UI at night (audit DSP-04)

premortem.title: Distraction: touching the screen while driving
premortem.fix: Nothing needs touch while moving; camera view only on blinker or danger; the beeps stop by themselves (a danger episode after 4 s), so you never reach for a mute

premortem.title: A video screen visible to the driver is illegal
premortem.fix: Camera views for manoeuvring are generally allowed (e.g. California VC 27602(b)(4)); no entertainment video. Check your state

premortem.title: Touch-only controls: no way to silence an alarm while the Pi boots (20–35 s) or after it crashes; gloves
premortem.fix: Every alarm silences itself on the ESP32, with or without the Pi: a danger episode beeps at once and after 3 s and is quiet from 4 s (the LED keeps flashing), a TPMS warning reminds twice, a fault beeps once. Touch mutes the rest: the Pi sends a mute counter in every $BSM line, and the ESP32 acts on it even if the vision loop has frozen. J4 keeps a spare button input (IO4)

premortem.title: Phantom touches or a cracked glass from a bezel that presses on it
premortem.fix: The TS-7 hangs on its 4 ear holes (M3 × 6 into the bezel's bosses), so the glass carries no load; the lip sits 0.3 mm in front of the glass, covers its outer 2 mm and stays ≥ 1.8 mm outside the active area (estimated: check after assembly)

premortem.title: Black screen after a cold start: the Pi looks for the display before the TS-7's scaler answers, or touch doesn't enumerate
premortem.fix: Both start on the same 5 V rail, so the display is powered no later than the Pi (SunFounder asks for USB power before HDMI). If B7 shows a black screen: video=HDMI-A-1:1024x600@60D in cmdline.txt (the D forces the connector on)

premortem.title: The display doesn't fit: shifter in P/R/N/D/M, your hand, the HVAC knobs
premortem.fix: 1:1 template + a foam block the size of the enclosure's rear box. The bezel is 129.0 mm tall, the opening's full height: its top sits at the opening's top edge (0 mm margin, checked by the generator), so it doesn't climb onto the HVAC panel; the opening's height comes from the v1 paper fit, so confirm it on the mock-up. The unit stands 21.8 mm proud of the trim (the Official display's design: 13 mm): check the shifter in every position

premortem.title: The enclosure's rear box (112 × 124 × 51 mm) is deeper than the pocket or hits the car's USB/12 V strip, which sits behind the panel ~34 mm below the top of the opening
premortem.fix: Measure ≥ 56 mm clear depth (55.5 needed) with the mock-up. The car's USB is reached through the v1 passthrough in the USB wing: its cable drops through the plate's slot and plugs into the car's port in the pocket, so the port itself stays hidden. If the depth isn't there: the PCB goes in its own box (same 92 × 92 posts) and the enclosure gets shallower

premortem.title: Printed parts warp or creep in the heat
premortem.fix: You can print: ASA or ABS (enclosed printer), or order MJF PA12 from JLC3DP with the PCB. PETG only for the test fit: its heat-deflection temperature (68–78 °C) is about the cabin air of a car parked all day in a hot climate, and the plate carries the display. Never PLA (55–60 °C). Heat-set brass inserts where screws are opened often (audit ENC-04, ENC-05)

premortem.title: The display comes loose in a crash or on bumps
premortem.fix: The TS-7 bolts to the bezel through its 4 ear holes and the bezel to the housing with 6 × M3; the lip also holds the glass if the tape between the LCD and its board lets go. The housing bolts to the car via the AMPS M4 nuts or a pocket bracket, never tape only; no sharp edges; nothing in airbag zones

premortem.title: Vibration loosens sockets and connectors
premortem.fix: Screw terminals for power, latching JST-GH for signals, strain relief, machined sockets + a dab of RTV (v1 rule), nylon lock nuts

premortem.title: Cracking the mirror cap while drilling, or drilling into the turn repeater or its wires
premortem.fix: Take the cap off (or look inside with a light) and mark the repeater and its wires first; practise on a used mirror cap; step drill; measure the camera barrel first; check the repeater still flashes (audit VEH-06)

premortem.title: Water in the camera, the door or the footwell
premortem.fix: O-ring + neutral-cure (oxime) RTV, drip loop, silicone grease only on the boot, reseal the door's vapour barrier with butyl after routing

premortem.title: Cables break in the mirror hinge or the door boot, or are caught by the window glass or its regulator
premortem.fix: Service loop; follow and tie to the factory harness on the door's inner (dry) side, above the glass's travel and clear of the regulator and lock rods; cycle door / window / mirror 50 times after the install (audit VEH-04)

premortem.title: Cables snag the pedals, the steering column or the seat rails
premortem.fix: Tie them up high along existing harnesses; never splice into the yellow SRS harness

premortem.title: The enclosure is drawn from estimates: SunFounder publishes no drawing of the TS-7 and its listed height (121.0 mm) disagrees with its photos (~124.4 mm over the ears); the ear holes, sockets, back-part height and plug sizes come from photos too. Straight Dupont plugs stand ~22 mm on the Pi's GPIO and would hit the PCB, so the Pi link uses your 40-pin ribbon's IDC (~12.5 mm)
premortem.fix: All of them are parameters: measure them (enclosure README, Measure first), lay the display on the template's page 1, --set, regenerate, and the 63 checks re-run. The bosses must match the ear holes within ~0.3 mm. Print the bezel first (~2 h) as a fit test

premortem.title: Screws through the display's ears crack its board or press on the glass
premortem.fix: M3 × 6 from behind through the ears into Ø7 bosses that touch only the ears, clear of the board's main edge (checked by the generator); M3 × 8 would reach the bezel's front face. Snug, not tight: it's a PCB

premortem.title: Fingers reach the boards through vents (Raspberry Pi docs: the enclosure must make the boards unreachable)
premortem.fix: Bezel intake slots 2.5 mm; the plate's windows are behind the display; fan grille with 2.5 mm gaps; split grommet in the cable exit

premortem.title: The camera USB plugs, the display leads and the antenna lead don't fit beside the box in the pocket
premortem.fix: Three 90° USB-A adapters (two cameras, the touch lead) and an SMA bulkhead. The display's flat cable and micro-USB lead rise inside the bezel to a 12.2 × 24 mm slot in the plate, inside the opening; both car-USB passthrough cables go down the same slot. The generator checks the plugs, the leads and the slot inside the opening's outline (2.6 mm margin at the tightest point)

premortem.title: The HDMI flat cable cracks at its fold, or its adapters or the micro-USB plug work loose on bumps
premortem.fix: One fold, made once, never creased back; Kapton tape over the adapters' latches; a dab of RTV on each plug once the picture is good (v1 socket rule); the leads tied to the plate's slot so they can't pull on the plugs

premortem.title: The two USB passthroughs don't fit their twin wing: thread Ø25.16 and double-D flats 23.28 are measured from your caliper photos, but collar, rear length (22.4), nut (36), cable (5.5) and plug (16.5 × 8.5) are still from the v1 3-D model
premortem.fix: Every size is a parameter (PASS_*): measure the remaining dimensions, regenerate, and the checks re-run (both Ø25.8 × 23.8 double-D cuts, both nuts spinning on the bench and clearing the trim, plug #2 passing alongside cable #1 through the side opening and plate slot)

premortem.title: No room for the twin USB wing on the trim right of the console opening (a vent, the glovebox, curved trim, the passenger's knee), or its front, 15.1 mm proud of the bezel, is in the way
premortem.fix: Tape a 33 × 81 mm cardboard wing to the trim during the mock-up. TRIM_RIGHT records the free space and the check fails if the wing doesn't fit

premortem.title: The piezo inside the unit is too quiet behind the slots, or it blocks the intake air
premortem.fix: Three fingers hold its face 2 mm off the skin behind five slots (~148 mm² open), so the sound and the air both pass (checked by the generator); bench test with the fan on and the windows up; BUZ_GAP=1 or a louder part of the same size if needed

premortem.title: No 12 V turn-signal wire found at the kick panel
premortem.fix: Best tap: each mirror's LED turn-signal repeater feed, in the door harness at the mirror connector: it runs where the camera cable and the LED pair already go through the door boot, one side per mirror. Confirm the wire with the wiring diagram (Toyota service information, techinfo.toyota.com, short subscriptions) and a meter (flashing 12 V with that side's signal and the hazards, dead otherwise). Fallbacks: the kick-panel feed, or the rear amber turn bulbs (WY21W, separate from the brake lamps per the owner's manual). Phase 2: CAN

premortem.title: The body control module drives the lamps with PWM; a simple input sees noise
premortem.fix: The detector bridges PWM gaps up to 25 ms and needs 50 ms to count, so PWM reads as a steady flash and spikes are ignored

premortem.title: Hazards cause a danger beep (both sides look like turns), including hazards pressed during a turn signal
premortem.fix: Hazards are both lamps lit at the same time for 50 ms; a turn signal never lights both. A side is reported only 150 ms after its lamp edge and while the other lamp is dark, so hazards (also pressed mid-flash during a turn signal) never read as a turn to either side, and after hazards end a side is reported only after a fresh flash. The first version used "both lit within 150 ms", which read some mid-flash presses as the other side (audit FW-01)

premortem.title: The added load trips bulb-out detection (fast flash)
premortem.fix: Each opto input draws ~6 mA

premortem.title: Our electronics desensitise the 315 MHz key fob receiver
premortem.fix: ACC-only: everything is off when you use the fob

premortem.title: CAN not on the OBD port, or behind a gateway
premortem.fix: Doesn't matter for the speed: OBD-II requires every car to answer standard requests such as PID 0x0D at the port. Only the phase-2 CAN cross-check needs the broadcasts on pins 6/14: check with a filtered sniff (B8)

premortem.title: A blinker input stuck lit (failed opto, shorted input, the wrong wire, or a combined brake/turn lamp tapped at the rear) reads as a permanent turn: nuisance danger beeps, and hazards read as a turn
premortem.fix: A lamp lit for more than 1.5 s without a break is an input fault: that side counts as dark, shows the fault pattern, one fault beep, and no danger beeps until it clears (dark for 2 s). Tap the front or kick-panel feed, not a combined rear lamp (audit FW-04)

premortem.title: The blinker is read from the dongle instead of the lamp wires, and a dropped Bluetooth link looks like "not signalling": no danger beep, silently
premortem.fix: Standard OBD-II has no turn-signal data; the lamps exist only as a Mazda-private broadcast (0x9A). The blinker stays on the opto taps (G9); OBD is used for the speed only. A CAN blinker is at most a phase-2 cross-check on a wired, listen-only adapter

premortem.title: The ELM327 is asked to listen to the bus (AT MA) and overflows
premortem.fix: Datasheet: a 512-byte buffer, and at the 38.4 kbaud a typical Bluetooth clone uses inside, printing one frame takes ~5.2 ms, while a 40 %-loaded 500 kbit/s bus delivers one every ~0.35 ms: BUFFER FULL. Monitoring also blocks requests. The firmware only *requests* PID 0x0D (010D1), one at a time

premortem.title: The dongle sleeps, hangs, answers ? or NO DATA, or the link drops; the speed goes stale
premortem.fix: 1 s timeouts, a reset (ATZ) after 3 failures, plain 010D for clones without the response-count digit, reconnect. NO DATA (key in ACC) is not a failure; any reset banner is accepted; a protocol search (SEARCHING...) gets 8 s; a reply delayed in the Bluetooth link is not taken for the next one's (audit FW-11/12). OBD speed counts only while < 1 s old; then the GPS takes over, then the 10 s hold, then LEDs only

premortem.title: Flat battery: the dongle is powered from OBD pin 16, always on. ELM327 datasheet: "about as much current as a dome lamp" (29.8 mA for its reference circuit, 17.6 mA in low-power mode)
premortem.fix: Measure its parked current (B8). Keep it plugged in only if it sleeps below ~5 mA; otherwise unplug it when parked for days, or use an OBD extension with a switch

premortem.title: Anyone in Bluetooth range connects with the default PIN and injects CAN frames: mazda_ic_mover moves this car's cluster needles with one 0x202 frame
premortem.fix: A dongle that needs a button press to pair, or sleeps its radio when parked; change the PIN if it allows; unplug it for long parking. The ESP32 itself only sends the setup AT commands and 010D

premortem.title: Bluetooth on the ESP32 disturbs the 315 MHz decoder's edge interrupt or the 1 kHz loop
premortem.fix: Bluetooth stack on core 0; the RF edge interrupt (rf_capture.cpp) and the 1 kHz loop on core 1. B8 compares the TPMS decode rate with the link on and off

premortem.title: The Pi would be the natural Bluetooth host, but its Bluetooth is off (dtoverlay=disable-bt: the PL011 UART carries the ESP32 link)
premortem.fix: The ESP32 talks to the dongle: the WROOM-32 has Bluetooth Classic. Connect by MAC address (a name search takes seconds), PIN usually 1234 or 0000. No change on the Pi or the PCB

premortem.title: The dongle is BLE-only (if it works with an iPhone, it is BLE or Wi-Fi), so Bluetooth Classic serial can't reach it
premortem.fix: Identify it first. The client logic doesn't depend on the transport: a BLE dongle needs a GATT client (NimBLE) instead of BluetoothSerial; a Wi-Fi one is out (the ESP32's Wi-Fi stays off)

premortem.title: A long dongle or an extension at the driver's knee catches a foot or a knee
premortem.fix: Low-profile dongle, or a short right-angle extension tied up out of the footwell

premortem.title: The 433 MHz-tuned radio loses ~10 dB at 315 MHz; rear wheels drop out
premortem.fix: Most of that loss is the antenna: a 433 MHz quarter-wave whip used at 315 MHz loses 9.5–11.7 dB, while the module's 433 MHz matching costs only ~0.2–0.5 dB if it follows TI's reference (audit RF-09). Use a 315 MHz quarter-wave antenna (~23 cm). A 315 MHz-tuned module with the same 2 × 4 pinout (~$3) is worth it only if an RSSI A/B test shows a gain. Check RSSI per wheel

premortem.title: The Pi 4, its USB 3 ports, the display and the regulator raise the 315 MHz noise floor; the TS-7's HDMI flat cable is unshielded and carries broadband TMDS data at ~0.5 Gb/s per lane
premortem.fix: The antenna leaves the enclosure: CC1101 → short RG316 → SMA bulkhead in the box wall → 30 cm RG316 → whip away from the Pi; cameras on the USB 2.0 ports; ferrites. Buy a shielded HDMI flat cable if you can find one; keep it short and away from the CC1101 and its lead. Compare the noise floor with everything on and off

premortem.title: The EG53MA4 decoder fails on real frames
premortem.fix: Decodes 64 of 64 real frames from rtl_433's SDR captures (audit), and on the bench the CC1101 decoded live 315 MHz frames sent by a USRP B205mini (bench log). Still untested with your own sensors: drive with rtl_433 -f 315M first (v1 premortem step 1)

premortem.title: Nuisance alerts in parking lots, drive-thrus and queues
premortem.fix: No alerts below 8 mph, on again at 12 mph (hysteresis); hazards silent; a danger episode goes quiet after 4 s and touch mute silences the current turn; at most one danger beep per 3 s, and a flickering detection can't beep more than once a second

premortem.title: GPS lost under a bridge or in a tunnel: alerts stop or go wild
premortem.fix: The car's own speed from the OBD dongle covers tunnels, garages and GPS cold starts. Without both, the last moving/slow decision is held 10 s; after that the LEDs keep working and the buzzer stays quiet

premortem.title: Trusting it: a missed motorcycle at night
premortem.fix: It is an aid: always look over your shoulder. Disclaimer on the start screen. Run the first month with the buzzer muted, logging every alert against what you see, so the miss and false-alarm rates are known before you rely on the beep (audit SAF-01)

premortem.title: A silent failure looks like "all clear"
premortem.fix: Fault pattern + one beep on a lost or frozen Pi link, a faulted camera, a stuck blinker input, or a Pi that never boots; per-side faults for the cameras and the blinker inputs (the camera-fault beep was promised but missing: audit FW-06)

premortem.title: The blind-spot beep is drowned out by a TPMS reminder or vice versa
premortem.fix: Priorities: danger, then fault, then TPMS. Each pattern plays for its full length; only a higher priority cuts it, and the cut one is played again. TPMS repeats at most every 10 minutes; a tyre hovering at the threshold re-raises the alarm once (audit FW-08/09)

premortem.title: The auto-mute hides a danger: you miss the first beeps, the car stays in your blind spot, the beep stops after 4 s
premortem.fix: The door LED keeps flashing as long as the danger lasts and the screen shows that camera; signalling again, or the lane clearing for 2 s and the danger coming back (another car), starts a new episode that beeps again. A flickering detection stays one episode

premortem.title: Scope creep: the project never finishes
premortem.fix: Ship in useful steps: (1) the camera view switches on the blinker, no AI; (2) detection, LEDs and buzzer; (3) CAN and the 60 GHz radar

premortem.title: Footprint errors (DevKit sockets, CC1101 socket, terminals)
premortem.fix: Print the assembly drawing 1:1 and set the real sockets and terminals on it before ordering, as for v1; the DevKit footprint carries both row spacings

premortem.title: Inventory entries are wrong or incomplete
premortem.fix: Collect every part before the layout freeze (G3)

premortem.title: Tools missing for the car work
premortem.fix: Multimeter, trim tools, solder-type USB-A plugs, step drill, heat gun: see the tools checklist in the viewer. No JST-GH crimper: the lab's elechawk pigtails come pre-crimped, and the PR-3254 does the Dupont ends

premortem.title: The enclosure becomes the long pole (~12 h of printing per try, ASA needs an enclosed printer)
premortem.fix: Parametric generator with fit checks; print the bezel first; foam mock-up before any printing; MJF PA12 as the no-printer route
